steps.title: Sunny or rainy?
steps.text: Listen to these two sounds. Which one sounds like a sunny day? Which one sounds like a rainy day?

steps.prompt: Does this one sound happy, or a bit sad?
steps.reveal: This one is a major chord. Lots of people say it sounds happy, like sunshine.
This one is a minor chord. Lots of people say it sounds a bit sad, like rain on the window.

steps.title: A chord is notes together
steps.text: A chord is a few notes played together. Old chips could only play a few notes at once. So composers played the notes one after another, super fast: a sparkle!

wow.text: Playing a chord's notes very fast, one after another, is called an arpeggio. Our ears hear it as one chord.

steps.intro: Sunny music: bounce! Rainy music: sway slowly.
Put four chord blocks in a row, then press Play. Play the pads on top!

steps.title: The Ending
steps.scenario: At the end of Moon Run, our robot gets home. But it says goodbye to its friend, who stays on the Moon. Should the ending music be happy, a bit sad, or both?
steps.reveal: Composers often mix happy and sad chords on purpose. Some people call it bittersweet. There's no right answer: it depends how you want players to feel.
steps.followUp: Can you think of a time you felt happy and a bit sad at the same time?

steps.intro: Make the chords for our game's song: four blocks in a row. Try them, then save them.

steps.title: A water-glass xylophone
need: Three jars or glasses, all the same
steps: Stand the jars a little apart.
A grown-up pours a little water in one and nearly fills another.
Tap each one gently with the pencil. Which one sounds higher?
steps.why: The jar with a little water sounds higher. The full jar sounds lower.
steps.safety: Glass can break: use plastic cups or jars, and let a grown-up do the pouring.

debrief: Which chord feels like you today?
